newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Aeroflot may remerge with some "babyflots".
newsitem.headline: Aeroflot may remerge with some "babyflots".

text.p: Russian international airline Aeroflot said on Tuesday it planned to remerge with some of the "babyflots" that split off after the collapse of communism.
Valery Okulov, Aeroflot's acting chief executive, told a news conference that several small regional carriers were willing to come back under the wing of the Russian commercial aviation giant.
On their own, they feared that they could not survive the rapidly changing domestic airlines market, he said.
Okulov said one airline had already accepted Aeroflot's offer. "Nizhegorodskiye airlines has decided to merge with Aeroflot," he said, without giving details.
Some airlines, however, were worried by the proposal, fearing Aeroflot may "eat" them, he said, adding that Aeroflot was not at war with regional airlines.

"We are opening new domestic routes...but that does not mean sharper competition with local carriers," he said, adding that the main target for Aeroflot was to compete with Western airlines which were expanding their routes to Russia.
"There are 337 carriers officially listed in Russia now, but many of them have serious financial problems. We want to help them survive," Okulov said.
The Federal Aviation Service, a state agency regulating civil aviation in Russia, said about 100 airlines went out of business due to lack of funds in 1996.

After the collapse of the Soviet Union in 1991, Aeroflot's divisions throughout the former superpower split off, even those within Russia. The numbers of "babyflots" were bolstered further by the establishment of new small private airlines.
Last week Aeroflot opened an office in Khabarovsk as the first stage in setting up a new hub in the Russian Far East.
Aeroflot plans to use Khabarovsk airport as a centre for its international and domestic cargo flights, including a new regular Moscow-Khabarovsk cargo route.

Aeroflot spokesman Alexander Luchaninov has said that the airline will start regular domestic passenger flights from Moscow to Kaliningrad, Krasnodar, Vladikavkaz, Vladivostok, Magadan, Chelyabinsk, Yekaterinburg and Nizhny Novgorod later this year.
The company makes scheduled flights from Moscow to 11 destinations in Russia and to former Soviet republics in the Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS).
